body.p: Claims 1-6 and 8-18 are pending in this application. The various parts of the Office Action (and other matters, if any) are discussed below under appropriate headings.
Examiner Interview
Applicant thanks the Examiner for participating in the telephone interview on August 29, 2024. Applicant's Interview Summary is encompassed within the following remarks.

During the interview, proposed amendments to claim 1 were discussed. The Examiner agreed that the proposed amendments would overcome the current rejection. The claims have been amended herein based on the amendments discussed during the interview.
Claims 1-6 and 8-16 stand rejected as being unpatentable over U.S. 2017/0245776 ("Kurtz") in view of U.S. 2018/0256097 ("Bray").
Independent Claim 1

Amended claim 1 recites a method performed by an anesthetizing monitoring unit configured to generate an improved evoked electromyography response signal. Claim 1 "generat[es] a single stimuli signal (Sstimuii) using the anesthetizing monitoring unit ... to stimulate a motor nerve of a patient." Claim 1 also "receiv[es] a single evoked electromyography, EMG, response signal (SResponse)."

With exemplary reference to Figure 3 below, claim 1 "estimat[es] a periodic noise waveform (Speriodic) based on a noise signal (SNoise) by splitting the noise signal (SNoise) into temporal segments." The "noise signal (SNoise) is caused by an electric power grid having a frequency." Also, "the temporal segments each have a periodic duration (TPeriodic) matching the frequency of the electric power grid."

Analysis: Amended Claim 1 Rejection
The cited reference combination does not disclose -as set forth in amended claim 1-"
" estimating a periodic noise waveform (Speriodic)... based on a noise signal (SNoise)
by splitting the noise signal (SNoise) into temporal segments, wherein:
o the noise signal (SNoise) is caused by an electric power grid having a
frequency;
o the temporal segments each have a periodic duration (TPeriodic)
matching the frequency of the electric power grid; and
o the temporal segments of the noise signal (SNoise) are detected during a
time interval (TNoise) not overlapping with a stimuli signal interval
(TStimulus) of the single stimuli signal (SStimuli) and not overlapping with
the duration of the response signal (TResponse)."

On page 4 of the Office Action the Examiner avers that Bray teaches the existence the independent claim i's "noise signal (Snoise) used during the estimating of the periodic noise waveform (Speriodic)."To support this conclusion, the Examiner points to paragraph [0057] of Bray, which teaches that these noise signals originate from "brief spontaneous contractions" "muscle fibers."

Claim 1's noise signal is a periodic noise represented by a periodic noise waveform that is caused by the electric power grid. (See, e.g., current application, paragraphs [0041] and [0064].) Conversely, Bray's "brief spontaneous contraction" produces, by definition, a brief spontaneous noise unrelated to the electric power grid.

Accordingly, claim 1 differs from Bray in that Bray avoids noise from muscle contractions, while claim 1 "reduce[s] noise in the response signal (SResponse) caused by the electric power grid." Claim 1 has been amended to clarify this distinction.
For at least the foregoing reasons, the cited reference combination does not disclose or render prima facie obvious the subject matter of amended claim 1 and the rejection

In view of the foregoing, Applicant requests issuance of a notice of allowance. Should the Examiner feel that a telephone interview would be helpful to facilitate favorable prosecution of the above-identified application, the undersigned invites the Examiner to contact the undersigned at the telephone number provided below.

The absence in this reply of any comments on any contentions set forth in the Office Action should not be construed to be an acquiescence therein. Rather, no comment is needed since the rejections should be withdrawn for at least the foregoing reasons.
Respectfully submitted,
